source:
let's make a car game that focuses on Holden vs Ford, but obviously with copyright free names.
we use "iron lion" as the Holden variant, and "blue wolf" as the ford variant, with trims being similar in letters, but the difference? the VE ute is a VA ute.
engines: Iron lion 5.0L V8 petrol (200kw, 300nm of torque) yes we will have power and torque specs here.. but in metric only with imperial measurements available in settings.
like a toggle.
obviously the standard reading is in kmh tho you can opt for mph or both at once, and the only drive side is right hand drive, this game takes the appearance of a new Zealand south island City (specifically eastern Christchurch around Buckley's road) turned into a sort of Roblox variant, where some locations are moved around so it doesn't replicate the real city too much, and the cars you get to actually see your character shifting gears, you can flick the indicator stalks even on mobile, and you can get a completely ai made instrumental version of copyrighted music to actually avoid copyright while having a jam.
for example, the song "jaded" by new Zealand based band racing, is a copyright protected song, so we use an instrumental different name for the song, calling it emeralded divinity.. but as an instrumental of that song.
tame impala - Dracula is then called tamed feline - vampire (instrumental, full)
each soundtrack spanning over 3 to 5 minutes.
anyways, on the car's interior, you get proper controls, and you even get a manual transmission interface when you hop into a manual iron lion vs an automatic iron lion which gives you a manual mode.
also, in the manuals, you get a clutch pedal.
which you can see your character use.
in the tutorial, it shows the pattern: clutch in, shift, apply throttle optionally, clutch out, repeat if needed.
you can even choose engines to swap into cars the more money you get via racing NPCs, racing players, or even just by playing the game or by playing a simulation using the car, or a "stop the lever In the green zone" minigame that always rewards you even if you lose it.
engines in this game include: diesel (inline 4, inline six, inline 5, V6, V8, V6 TT, V12 5.0L NA petrol, and many more petrols, like I3 to I9 and V2 to V28 (28L V28) located in a giant motorhome.
the starter car you get is based on a Toyota crown royal saloon 2.5L V6, it's the Toyokao Crow loyal salmon 2.5P 6AT.. or a manual altezza? it's the raltezzo SR200S beans, 87 octane to 100 octane petrols available mostly just 91 to 98 tho, and an Australian ford falcon XR6 twin turbo based copyright free ute appears.

answers.ask: Is this free-roam driving with optional street races, or are the races the main loop with a proper track?
answers.answer: This is free-roam driving in a Roblox-inspired eastern Christchurch, with optional races against NPCs and players as the main ways to earn money alongside normal play and simulation/minigames. Do not make a separate proper track the core loop.

answers.ask: How much of eastern Christchurch should the map cover, and which landmarks must be recognisable?
answers.answer: Keep it to a small, condensed area inspired by eastern Christchurch around Buckleys Road, with roads and locations moved around so it is not a replica. No real landmarks need to be recognisable; use a generic New Zealand South Island suburban-city look.

A: This is free-roam driving in a Roblox-inspired eastern Christchurch, with optional races against NPCs and players as the main ways to earn money alongside normal play and simulation/minigames. Do not make a separate proper track the core loop.
- [author] scale — Q: How much of eastern Christchurch should the map cover, and which landmarks must be recognisable? A: Keep it to a small, condensed area inspired by eastern Christchurch around Buckleys Road, with roads and locations moved around so it is not a replica. No real landmarks need to be recognisable; use a generic New Zealand South Island suburban-city look.
- [agent_inferred] first race footprint — Q: What is the narrowest street-race layout the first map needs? A: Use one optional point-to-point route over the existing roads, with no separate track.
- [agent_inferred] vehicle access — Q: What minimum free-roam start is needed? A: Provide one curbside player-car start connected directly to the road network.
- [agent_inferred] enclosure — Q: Do the first build’s buildings need enterable interiors? A: Keep them as exterior street frontage because the requested play is driving and no indoor activity was named.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a small condensed New Zealand South Island suburban-city driving map, loosely inspired by eastern Christchurch but with roads and locations rearranged so no real landmark or exact street plan is recognizable. Build a connected network of left-side-traffic roads sized for right-hand-drive cars, mixing suburban blocks and modest city streets with one curbside player-car start. Reuse part of the same street network for one optional point-to-point race, marked only by a modest start line and finish gate so the city remains a free-roam environment rather than a dedicated track. Keep all buildings exterior-only and frame the complete road network clearly.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Simulation because free-roam vehicle operation is the main space. Racing is secondary because optional NPC and player street races need physical start and finish placements.

## Shape and preset
Use `world-open` for one freely explored road network. Start from the Vehicle Sim preset, retain its shared-world shape and vehicle-width routes, and drop the unrelated shared resource field.

## Config requirements
Use `path-road-vehicle` routed as `P0` street circulation for connected left-side-traffic roads and `settlement-density` for the condensed suburban-city blocks. Use the visible halves of `startpoint-line`, `spawn-grid`, and `trigger-finish` for one understated optional street-race route. Do not add a separate circuit, recognizable real landmark, or enterable building.

## Layout requirements
Place one player-car `SpawnZone` with no canonical option ID at the curbside pull-off. Place the functional halves of `startpoint-line` and `trigger-finish` at opposite ends of one valid point-to-point route over existing streets, and use `spawn-grid` for two aligned race slots supporting the player and either an NPC or player opponent. Engine swaps, vehicle interiors, transmissions, controls, currency, minigames, units, and soundtrack add no map geometry.

## Layout components
One compact city contains connected roads, intersections, suburban blocks, modest city frontage, one player start, and one optional race route sharing the streets. Outer block faces form the boundary. The race must not prevent free circulation through the rest of the map.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: road connectivity and the optional point-to-point race must be valid before suburban-city dressing.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is medium, consisting of a condensed driveable district. The theme is a generic contemporary New Zealand South Island suburban city. Use `P6` because the selected race start and finish require one valid connected route.
